section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header for the maamar delivered on the last day of Pesach 5725.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
The last day of Pesach,
the year 5725.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verses describing Mashiach's coming, his personal quality, his leadership, and the resulting universal revelation of G-dliness.
section.t: "And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him... and he shall scent the fear of Hashem... and the wolf shall dwell with the lamb..."
And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, explains in his maamar beginning with the words "This"
that in these verses the prophet describes the coming of Mashiach our righteousness, who will come to redeem us speedily in our days,
and he states several things regarding King Mashiach and his conduct.
First, he explains the virtue of King Mashiach himself—"And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him,"
and afterwards he explains his conduct—"and he shall scent the fear of Hashem"
[for even "and he shall scent" is a matter of his conduct,
as in "he smells"
"and judges"],
and afterwards he adds "and the wolf shall dwell with the lamb,"
that the conduct of Mashiach will be in a manner that he will bring about
a revelation of G-dliness throughout the entire world,
not only in the speaking species but also in the living species
(wolf and leopard, etc.)
and even in the inanimate species,
and as the verse continues,
"For the earth shall be filled with knowledge of Hashem,"
that even the physical earth
(inanimate)
will be filled with knowledge of Hashem.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between the influence of a teacher and a king, their roots in Torah, and how Mashiach embodies both roles, revealing even transcendent matters as an encompassing light.
section.t: And the maamar points out,
that one must understand,
since the earth will then be filled with knowledge of Hashem,
why will a king be needed?
And the point of the explanation is
that kingship is a matter of exaltation,
that the king is separate and elevated from the people.
And even the commands of the king
(although ostensibly they are a movement of closeness,
that the king draws near to the people to lead them according to his will)
are
in a manner of elevation and separation,
in the way of a decree and command.
And so it is also from the side of the people,
that their fulfillment of the king's command is not because they know and comprehend the reason for the command,
but rather,
because of the fear and awe of the king,
that his awe be upon you.
Thus,
even the influence from the king to the people is in a manner of exaltation and separation.
And this is the difference between the influence of a teacher and the influence of a king,
that the matter of a teacher's influence is that the teacher draws close to the student
(contracting his intellect according to the vessel of the student)
in a way that the student will comprehend the intellect,
but not so the influence of a king, which is separate from the people,
above their intellect.
And the root of these two matters
(the influence of a teacher and of a king)
is
also in the Torah,
for there are in it
(analogous to)
these two matters.
For there are matters in the Torah that are clothed in intellect,
but the essence of the Torah is above intellect.
And in the future to come,
both matters will be revealed.
For this is why Mashiach is called by the name "teacher" and by the name "king,"
meaning,
that in addition to Mashiach teaching Torah to all of Israel
and influencing upon them good taste and knowledge in the secrets,
in the inner dimension of the Torah,
due to which influence Mashiach is called by the name "teacher,"
he himself will attain infinitely more than what he will influence in comprehension,
and the influence of these matters will be in the aspect of makif (encompassing light),
analogous to the influence of a king.
And one may add, seemingly,
that based on what is known
that the Torah study of Mashiach
(what he will teach all the people)
will be in a manner of vision that is above comprehension,
it is understood from this,
that the matters he will influence in the manner of a king are matters that cannot come into revelation even in a vision above intellect,
and nevertheless,
because Mashiach will be
(also)
a king,
he will reveal to Israel even these matters,
except that the revelation of these matters will be in the way of makif (encompassing light).
